name: Quarterly and annual financial reporting (single-mine gold producer)
summary: Each quarter the Toronto finance team turns the mine's month-end close and the head-office ledger into IFRS financial statements, an MD&A with non-IFRS cost measures such as all-in sustaining cost per ounce, and a results news release. The auditor reviews the quarterly statements and audits the annual ones, the audit committee approves them, and the CEO and CFO certify the filings before they go on SEDAR within 45 days of a quarter end or 90 days of the year end. The work is slow because head office waits one to two weeks for the remote site to close, the consolidation and MD&A are rolled forward in linked spreadsheets and Word files, and auditor and committee calendars set fixed dates.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed single-mine gold producer with an 11-person corporate finance team in Toronto, a site finance group at the mine and a mid-market ERP with spreadsheet consolidation.
baseline.notes: Clock starts at quarter end and stops at the conference call the morning after the release. One of the four reports a year is the annual report, which adds the audit; the annual information form is filed in parallel and belongs to corp-disclosure.

unit_of_work: one quarterly report (statements, MD&A, news release and certificates for one quarter or the year)
trigger: The quarter ends; the case becomes active when the site's quarter-end cost report and close package arrive about one to two weeks later.
end_state: Statements, MD&A and certificates are filed on SEDAR, the news release is out and the conference call is held.

volume.seasonality: Four reports a year, one per quarter. The year-end report (January to March) carries the audit and is about twice the work of a quarter.

evidence.note: NI 51-102 requires interim reports for each of the first three quarters and an annual report: four a year.
Copied from the organisation file: the annual audit and full statements take about twice the effort of a quarterly review. In this file the extra work is modelled by the year-end branch (s08-s09).
About 25-35 hours a quarter preparing the quarter-end package beyond the routine month-end close and answering corporate queries; the month-end close itself sits in site-cost-reporting.

Two corporate accountants spend roughly the first week after each quarter closing the head-office ledger and the last days preparing the filing; about 0.25 FTE of the pair across the year, more in January-March.

Three reporting accountants; quarterly and annual statements, non-IFRS reconciliations and audit support take a large share of their time in the 6-8 weeks after each quarter end. Rest of their time goes to the AIF, tax support and month-end analysis.
Quarterly income and mining tax provision, royalty accruals and gold sales reconciliation take about two weeks of effort each quarter.
The corporate controller owns the consolidation review, drafts the MD&A and manages the auditor; about 0.3 FTE averaged over the year for a single-mine producer.
Review of the full package, disclosure committee and audit committee meetings and the conference call; about 30-40 hours a quarter.
Operations commentary for the MD&A and sub-certification of site results, a few hours a quarter.

roles.title: Vice-president, investor relations and corporate development

evidence.note: Drafts and disseminates the results news release and prepares the conference call script.
Reviews forward-looking statement language and chairs or attends the disclosure committee.
Reviews the release, signs the certificate and leads the conference call.

systems.name: Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Newswire distribution service (results news release dissemination)

steps.name: Close head-office ledger
steps.description: Two corporate accountants post the head-office quarter-end entries in the ERP: accrued corporate G&A and legal fees, share-based compensation expense, interest on cash, bank reconciliations from the bank portals and FX revaluation of the US dollar gold proceeds account. The clock for the report starts at quarter end; they begin on the first business day.

error.defect_description: A missed accrual or wrong FX rate on the US dollar account.

evidence.note: Common corporate close practice for a TSX-listed single-asset producer; quarter end often falls on a weekend or before a holiday, so work starts 1-4 days after it.

steps.name: Receive site quarter-end close package
steps.description: The site controller sends the quarter-end package once the site month-end close is complete: site trial balance, monthly cost report by department, inventory valuation (ore stockpile, gold in circuit, doré in transit, supplies), capital spending by project and the accrual list. Head office waits for the site close, which takes about one to two weeks.

error.defect_description: In-circuit gold or stockpile values not updated for the latest reconciliation, an accrual missed, or capital development coded as operating cost.

evidence.note: Site month-end close of 7-12 business days at a remote mine with paper timesheets and a mid-market ERP; wait counted from the end of s01.

steps.name: Review site results and inventory valuation
steps.description: A reporting accountant opens the site package beside the prior quarter and the site forecast, ties ounces and tonnes to the production report, checks the inventory against net realisable value at the current gold price and checks the split between capitalised and expensed development and exploration. Anything unexplained goes back to the site controller as a query list.

error.defect_description: A misstatement in inventory or capitalisation is not spotted.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting certified by the CEO and CFO under NI 52-109: management review of subsidiary results

evidence.note: Management review control over site results expected under ICFR certification; split of capitalised development is a known judgment area at underground mines.

steps.name: Correct site entries and answer queries
steps.description: The site controller and a site accountant look up the queried items, post correcting journal entries in the ERP and email back a revised trial balance and explanations. Typical items are missed contractor accruals, stockpile tonnage after the survey and capital projects booked to operating cost centres.

error.defect_description: A correction posted to the wrong period or cost centre.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of query turnaround between a remote site and head office.

steps.name: Reconcile gold sales and prepare tax provision
steps.description: The treasury and tax manager reconciles ounces and revenue to refinery outturn statements and bullion bank sale confirmations, then calculates current and deferred income tax, Ontario mining tax and royalty accruals and revalues US dollar balances. Results go into the consolidation as journal entries with a support workbook.

error.defect_description: Tax pool or royalty base wrong, deferred tax on mining tax missed.

evidence.note: Common practice; deferred mining tax under the Ontario Mining Tax Act is a separate calculation at Ontario producers. Runs alongside the site review.

steps.name: Consolidate results
steps.description: A reporting accountant loads the site and head-office trial balances into the consolidation workbook, adds the Quebec care-and-maintenance property costs, eliminates intercompany balances, maps accounts to statement lines and ties cash and equity to the subledgers. The workbook is a chain of linked spreadsheets rolled forward from the prior quarter.

error.defect_description: A mapping or elimination error, a sign flip or a stale workbook link.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet consolidation is the common tool at a single-mine producer with two legal entities; no consolidation software assumed.

steps.name: Review consolidated results and variances
steps.description: The corporate controller compares every statement line with the prior quarter, the same quarter last year and budget, asks for explanations above the variance threshold and challenges the judgments on inventory value, capitalisation and provisions. Errors found go back for correction; for the fourth quarter the year-end audit work starts here.

error.defect_description: A variance accepted with a plausible but wrong explanation.

next.condition: first to third quarter: interim review

evidence.note: Controller review is the main detective control; one of four reports is annual, so 25% of cases that pass take the audit path.

steps.name: Prepare year-end audit support
steps.description: Two reporting accountants build the auditor's requested schedules: lead sheets, PP&E and mineral property roll-forward, depletion recalculated on the new reserve statement, update of the closure cost provision, impairment indicator assessment and inventory count support. They answer the auditor's request list as items come in.

error.defect_description: A schedule does not tie to the ledger, or depletion uses last year's reserve.

control.basis: NI 51-102 s.4.1(2): annual financial statements must be audited

evidence.note: NI 51-102 s.4.1(2) requires audited annual statements; the content and hours of the audit support are the author's estimate.

steps.name: External auditor year-end fieldwork
steps.description: The audit team tests balances at head office, follows up the inventory observation done at the mine, sends confirmations to banks and the refinery and raises queries and proposed adjustments. The finance team answers queries between its other work; the elapsed time is set by the audit plan.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Annual results for 2020 came out 69 days after year end against 34-41 days for quarters; most of the difference is the audit. Fieldwork length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft financial statements and notes
steps.description: Two reporting accountants roll forward last quarter's statements in Word and Excel, update the primary statements from the consolidation and rewrite the notes for inventory, mineral properties, provisions, share capital, tax and commitments, then cross-reference every number to the workbook.
outputs: draft condensed interim or annual statements

error.defect_description: A note figure that no longer agrees with the primary statements after a late change.

evidence.note: Wesdome's quarterly statements are unaudited condensed interim statements; the drafting method and hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Calculate non-IFRS cost measures
steps.description: A third reporting accountant calculates cash cost and all-in sustaining cost per ounce sold, mine operating profit, EBITDA and free cash flow, and builds the reconciliations to the IFRS statement lines. Sustaining and growth capital are split project by project following the World Gold Council guidance.

error.defect_description: Capital classified as growth instead of sustaining, understating AISC.

evidence.note: Wesdome reported ten non-IFRS measures in Q2 2022, with AISC following the WGC guidance note; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft MD&A
steps.description: The corporate controller rolls forward the prior MD&A: highlights, operating results by mine, financial results, liquidity and capital, performance against guidance, risks, controls and the forward-looking statements caution. Numbers are typed in from the consolidation and the non-IFRS tables.

error.defect_description: An MD&A figure typed from an earlier version of the consolidation.

evidence.note: Each Wesdome results release refers readers to the quarter's MD&A for non-IFRS reconciliations; NI 51-102 Part 4A sets the forward-looking language. Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write operations commentary
steps.description: The mine general manager writes the paragraphs on underground development, stoping, mill throughput, recovery and safety for the quarter, and checks the production numbers quoted in the MD&A against site records.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Site input to the MD&A is common at single-mine producers; the GM gives a sub-certification on site results.

steps.name: Auditor reviews draft statements and MD&A
steps.description: For the first three quarters the auditor performs a review (inquiry and analytical procedures) of the interim statements; for the fourth quarter it completes the audit. The audit team reads the MD&A for consistency and sends a list of comments and proposed adjustments.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: Auditor interim review (CPA Canada Handbook review engagement standard); NI 51-102 s.4.3(3) notice if not reviewed

evidence.note: NI 51-102 s.4.3(3) requires a notice if interim statements were not reviewed by an auditor, so listed producers normally engage a review. Turnaround is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Clear auditor comments
steps.description: A reporting accountant posts agreed adjustments in the consolidation, updates the statement drafts and answers each point on the auditor's list in writing. A material adjustment means the statements and MD&A must be redrafted.

error.defect_description: An adjustment posted in the workbook but not carried to the notes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; most review comments are presentation points.

steps.name: CFO reviews full package
steps.description: The CFO reads the statements, MD&A and non-IFRS reconciliations together, checks the messaging against guidance and the market's expectations and collects sub-certifications from the controllers and the GM. MD&A sections that do not explain the quarter go back for rewriting.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: Disclosure controls and procedures (NI 52-109): CFO review and sub-certification

evidence.note: CFO review before disclosure committee is common practice; the CFO signs the NI 52-109 certificate.

steps.name: Draft results news release
steps.description: The vice-president of investor relations builds the news release from the MD&A: headline numbers, tables, non-IFRS cautions, outlook against guidance and the conference call details, and drafts the call script.

error.defect_description: A release figure differs from the MD&A after a late change.

evidence.note: Release structure follows Wesdome's results releases; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Disclosure committee and legal review
steps.description: The general counsel reviews the MD&A and release for forward-looking statements, cautionary language and the stated assumptions, and the disclosure committee (CEO, CFO, general counsel, investor relations, controller) meets to walk through the package and agree the wording.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: NI 51-102 Part 4A requires a reasonable basis, cautionary language and material assumptions for forward-looking information; the committee format is common practice.

steps.name: Send audit committee package
steps.description: The corporate controller assembles the statements, MD&A, news release, auditor's review or audit report draft and certificates into the audit committee package and sends it to the committee members about a week before the meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Common governance practice; meeting materials go out several days ahead.

steps.name: Audit committee reviews and approves
steps.description: The audit committee meets on its scheduled date with the CFO, controller and auditor, hears the auditor's report, questions judgments and approves the interim statements and MD&A under delegated authority; for the year end it recommends the statements and the full board approves them the same day.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: NI 51-102 ss.4.5 and 5.5: board (or audit committee for interim) approval before filing

evidence.note: NI 51-102 ss.4.5 and 5.5: the board approves statements and MD&A before filing and may delegate interim approval to the audit committee. Meeting lead time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: CEO and CFO sign certificates
steps.description: The CEO and CFO sign the NI 52-109 certificates for the interim or annual filings, relying on the sub-certifications and the controller's control testing summary.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

control.basis: NI 52-109 Certification of Disclosure in Issuers' Annual and Interim Filings

evidence.note: NI 52-109 certification of annual and interim filings (instrument text not opened).

steps.name: File on SEDAR
steps.description: A corporate accountant converts the approved statements, MD&A and certificates to PDF and files them on SEDAR before the news release goes out, checking the filing types and the issuer profile.

error.defect_description: Wrong document type selected or a page missing from the PDF.

evidence.note: NI 51-102 ss.4.2 and 4.4: annual statements within 90 days and interim within 45 days for a non-venture issuer.

steps.name: Disseminate news release
steps.description: Investor relations releases the results through the newswire after market close, posts the release, statements and MD&A on the company website and emails the analyst list.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Wesdome released results after market close with a call the next morning.

steps.name: Hold results conference call
steps.description: The next morning at 10:00 the CEO, CFO and COO present the quarter on a call and webcast and take analysts' questions; investor relations logs follow-up questions.

error.defect_description: None introduced at this step.

evidence.note: Calls at 10:00 am ET the day after the release for Q3 2020 and FY2020.

exceptions.name: Site corrections after head-office review
exceptions.description: The reporting accountant's review finds missed accruals, stale inventory values or miscoded capital; the site posts corrections and resends.

exceptions.name: Year-end audit
exceptions.description: The fourth-quarter report carries the annual audit: audit support schedules, depletion on the new reserve, closure provision update, impairment indicators and two to three weeks of auditor fieldwork.

exceptions.name: MD&A rewrite after CFO review
exceptions.description: The CFO finds the MD&A does not explain the quarter's cost or grade story and sends it back for rewriting.

exceptions.name: Material audit adjustment
exceptions.description: The auditor proposes an adjustment large enough that statements, non-IFRS tables and MD&A are redrafted.

exceptions.name: Audit committee asks for changes
exceptions.description: The committee asks for wording or disclosure changes in the MD&A before approving.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from period end to results release
benchmarks.population: Wesdome Gold Mines: Q3 2020 (34 days), Q2 2022 (41 days), FY2020 (69 days)

evidence.note: Release dates are published; p50 is the midpoint of the two quarters opened and p90 is the annual report, since one report in four is annual.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days after interim period end
calendar days after financial year end

evidence.note: Mine operating profit, mining and processing costs, cash costs, cash margin, AISC, cost per tonne milled, adjusted net income, EBITDA, operating cash flow per share, free cash flow.

pain_points.description: Head office waits one to two weeks for the remote site to close before consolidation can start, which uses a quarter of the 45-day window.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of site close time with paper timesheets and manual inventory valuation.

pain_points.description: Consolidation, non-IFRS tables and MD&A are linked spreadsheets and Word files rolled forward each quarter; a late change has to be retyped in several places and figures drift between documents.

evidence.note: Common at small issuers without disclosure management software in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Sustaining versus growth capital classification drives AISC, the measure analysts watch most, and is decided project by project late in the cycle.

evidence.note: WGC guidance leaves classification to management judgment; AISC is a headline measure in each Wesdome release.

pain_points.description: Auditor review slots and the audit committee date are fixed in advance; any slippage in drafting compresses the time for review rather than moving the date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice.

assumptions: The cycle is measured from quarter end to the conference call; the site month-end close itself belongs to site-cost-reporting and appears here only as the wait in s02.

One report in four is annual: the 21% branch at s07 (25% of cases that pass the review) adds audit support and auditor fieldwork. The annual information form, filed on the same 90-day deadline, is in corp-disclosure and not modelled.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage times 1.30 for office and staff roles; executive cash compensation only).
The auditor and the audit committee are external parties; their time carries no labour cost in this file, and their elapsed time is mostly in wait_before_min.
Steps with people = 2 (s01, s08, s10) are two people in the same role working in parallel; touch_min is elapsed working time.

The simulated median of about 39 days and p90 of about 65 days sit close to the Wesdome release dates opened (34 and 41 days for quarters, 69 days for the 2020 year end); the simulated p90 is a few days short because the year-end branch is drawn for about a quarter of cases and the slowest year ends are not modelled.

Roles state about 1.9 FTE against about 0.8 FTE implied by step hands-on time. The gap is deliberate: the stated FTE includes time the steps do not itemise, such as answering auditor queries between steps, the monthly analysis that feeds the quarter, internal control testing for the certificates and preparation for audit committee questions.

The organisation file lists only five roles for this process; this file adds treasury-tax-manager (tax provision and gold sales reconciliation), gm (operations commentary), vp-ir (news release), general-counsel (disclosure review) and ceo (certificate and call), all of which exist in the organisation file.

Interfaces add two inputs not in the organisation file entry (production_report from mill-met-accounting for ounces sold, reserve_statement from ts-reserve-estimate for year-end depletion) and the news_release output to shareholders and osc-tsx.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.

sources.title: National Instrument 51-102 Continuous Disclosure Obligations (consolidated text)
sources.publisher: British Columbia Securities Commission (Canadian Securities Administrators instrument)
sources.supports: s.4.1(2) annual statements must be audited; s.4.2 non-venture issuers file audited annual statements within 90 days of year end; s.4.3(3) interim statements not reviewed by an auditor must carry a notice saying so; s.4.4 interim statements within 45 days of period end; s.4.5 board approves annual and interim statements before filing and may delegate interim approval to the audit committee; s.5.5 the same for MD&A; s.6.2 AIF within 90 days; Part 4A forward-looking information needs a reasonable basis, cautionary language and the material assumptions; Part 4B FOFI and financial outlooks. The consolidation opened shows no version date; it uses pre-IFRS wording ('interim financial statements') and already contains Parts 4A and 4B. The 45-day and 90-day deadlines and the approval rules were unchanged in 2019-2022.
